reuse.why: Adds a shared skipsWeekendOccurrences predicate and still calls applyWeekendRule, but each site wraps that rule with its own skip-or-move decision instead of extending the tree's single weekend-rule definition.

duplication.why: The 'daily + skip -> drop weekend occurrences, otherwise move' logic is written three times: pickDate/take=7 in getNextDate, over-fetch/filter/slice in getUpcomingDates, and resolveDate plus an isWeekend guard in createScheduleList.

placement.why: The predicate lands in shared/schedules.ts next to applyWeekendRule, but the actual occurrence-dropping lives in server call sites rather than in the shared schedule logic.

scope.why: Edits are on the weekend-handling paths plus carrying frequency through parseRecurDate, a test and a release note.

maintainability.why: The comment 'the single definition of the weekend rule' is no longer true: the next change to weekend handling must be made consistently in three hand-rolled variants with different look-ahead heuristics (7 vs count*7).

bypasses_abstraction.where: getUpcomingDates (server/schedules/app.ts) and createScheduleList (server/budget/schedule-template.ts) apply their own weekend filtering around applyWeekendRule/applyWeekendRuleToDay instead of a shared occurrence rule

disguised_duplication.where: the weekend-occurrence skip appears as pickDate in getNextDate, as filter/slice in getUpcomingDates and as an isWeekend guard on monthlyTarget in createScheduleList

one_place.where: only the 'does this schedule skip' predicate is shared (skipsWeekendOccurrences in shared/schedules.ts); the skip itself is implemented separately in getNextDate, getUpcomingDates and createScheduleList
